def.brief: Amend and add tests in test_dwitbuk.py for Q-bounded (the latest root direction; read that section and the two paragraphs it supersedes). (a) In test_Q_raw_text_a_conflict_sorting_after_a_modified_file_keeps_one_calls_order_with_diff_cc_first, remove only the exact cross-batch global order requirement: keep asserting, at every batch limit where the text is not cut, that each kept section (the diff --cc of the UU path and the modified file's) is present exactly once with all its source content. (b) Point the tests that observe or inject path_diff's content diff calls (unattributable_git, recorded_git and their users) at the new seam dwitbuk.git_patch(target, *args) or at subprocess invocation, keeping their assertions. (c) Add a focused cap regression on a real repository: enough changed source files, with PATHSPEC_BATCH_BYTES lowered so they need many batches and their diffs pass the 80000-character cut early; instrument at subprocess invocation (wrap subprocess.run and count the git diff content calls) and assert that after the batch whose sections pass the cut no further git diff batch is invoked, diff_truncated is true, the diff begins with git's first path, and no section repeats. (d) Add a test that the generic dwitbuk.git keeps its previous newline semantics while dwitbuk.git_patch returns git's bytes untranslated, on a real CR-containing file. Keep the DU/UD, raw-CR, conflict, git-config and exact-section tests otherwise as they are; do not copy the parser's logic into tests. Show the new and amended tests failing on the current tree where they should (focused python3 -c runs; never python3 -m unittest). No mutation campaign. Change no file but test_dwitbuk.py; do not commit.

non-claims: no check decides this task; done means the agent said so

(provider) The amended order test (item 3, 'when the text is not cut every kept section is present exactly once with all its source content') passes on the current tree: it is a relaxation of a test that already passed, so it cannot fail before the build.

(provider) 'Patches of batches not yet needed are never kept' is decided only by observation at subprocess.run: a build that runs later batches through another path (Popen, os.system) and throws them away would get past the call count. No test can see memory that is kept and then dropped.

(provider) 'used only by path_diff's content diff calls': the tests check that eyes-request content calls go through git_patch and that injecting at git_patch reaches both eyes request and excluded_diff. No test checks that no other caller uses git_patch.

(provider) The cap tests compare the decoded stdout length of each git diff call with the limit. That equals the composed text only when no section is filtered out, which holds in these fixtures (no declared record among the paths in the eyes test; all records in the excluded test).

(provider) 'Unexpected output fails explicitly before any packet is written' and the Q-git-config canonical flags are decided by the existing tests, now pointed at git_patch. The git-config tests themselves were not changed.

response.summary:
I amended and added tests in test_dwitbuk.py for Q-bounded; no other file changed and nothing is committed. The full check `python3 test_dwitbuk.py` gives 8 failures on the current tree, and every one is a Q-bounded test failing for the right reason. Six fail because dwitbuk.git_patch, the new patch helper, does not exist yet. The excluded_diff cap test fails because all 40 batches are still read. The eyes cap test also fails on the missing seam. When I stood in a temporary git_patch in memory, it then failed because all 60 batches were still read. Under the same stand-in, the generic git() helper failed its universal-newline check, because the current helper no longer translates line endings. All other tests pass.

(a) I renamed the order test to test_Q_bounded_raw_text_a_conflict_sorting_after_a_modified_file_keeps_each_section_once_whole_at_every_limit. It no longer requires one call's global order across batches. At each of 8 batch limits it checks that the UU file's diff --cc section and d.py's section each appear exactly once and whole, with nothing else in the text. With no batch limit lowered, it still requires the exact text of one unbatched git diff call. It passes now, which is expected because it is a relaxation.

(b) recorded_git now wraps both dwitbuk.git and dwitbuk.git_patch, and unattributable_git injects at git_patch. Both first check that git_patch exists, and their users' assertions are unchanged.

(c) Two cap tests on real repositories, counted at subprocess.run: eyes request with 60 large files (cut at 80000 characters) and excluded_diff with 40 large records (cut at 40000). Each checks that the last git diff call made is the one whose output passes the cut, the text is cut at the limit, starts with git's first path, is the beginning of git's own text and has no repeated section. The eyes test also checks diff_truncated is true and that every content call went through git_patch. In the current tree each path gets its own git diff call even at a limit sized for two, so the count bound is "fewer calls than paths". The sum check is what decides the cap.

(d) A test on a real file containing CRs, CRLFs and an invalid UTF-8 byte: git() returns text with universal newlines, git_patch returns git's bytes decoded without translation, and both return None when git exits non-zero.
non-claims: The amended order test (item 3, 'when the text is not cut every kept section is present exactly once with all its source content') passes on the current tree: it is a relaxation of a test that already passed, so it cannot fail before the build.

'Patches of batches not yet needed are never kept' is decided only by observation at subprocess.run: a build that runs later batches through another path (Popen, os.system) and throws them away would get past the call count. No test can see memory that is kept and then dropped.

'used only by path_diff's content diff calls': the tests check that eyes-request content calls go through git_patch and that injecting at git_patch reaches both eyes request and excluded_diff. No test checks that no other caller uses git_patch.

The cap tests compare the decoded stdout length of each git diff call with the limit. That equals the composed text only when no section is filtered out, which holds in these fixtures (no declared record among the paths in the eyes test; all records in the excluded test).

'Unexpected output fails explicitly before any packet is written' and the Q-git-config canonical flags are decided by the existing tests, now pointed at git_patch. The git-config tests themselves were not changed.
